text: Suppose a backup copy of the heeyID database leaves the bank on a disk.
prefix: Suppose a backup copy of the heeyID database leaves the bank on a disk.

text: Nobody should have taken it.
prefix: Nobody should have taken it.

text: On it are the customers of the bank: names, passport data, addresses and phone numbers.
prefix: On it are the customers of the bank: names, passport data, addresses and phone numbers.

text: Aziz is one of them.
prefix: Aziz is one of them.

text: What can the person with the disk read?
prefix: What can the person with the disk read?

text: Lesson 5 showed the adapters that talk to MyID, TAF, the SMS vendor and the push service.
prefix: Lesson 5 showed the adapters that talk to MyID, TAF, the SMS vendor and the push service.

text: Each adapter takes its credential from Vault.
prefix: Each adapter takes its credential from Vault.

text: Now Vault opens, and the keys inside it answer the question of the disk.
prefix: Now Vault opens, and the keys inside it answer the question of the disk.

text: Vault is a safe for keys, and it runs inside the bank.
prefix: Vault is a safe for keys, and it runs inside the bank.

text: Each zone gets its own new Vault.
prefix: Each zone gets its own new Vault.

text: The security team of the bank holds the keys that unlock it.
prefix: The security team of the bank holds the keys that unlock it.

text: The vendor that wrote heeyID never sees one of them.
prefix: The vendor that wrote heeyID never sees one of them.

text: This is the line in the design that matters most: the bank keeps the keys.
prefix: This is the line in the design that matters most: the bank keeps the keys.

text: Vault holds nine kinds of keys for each zone.
prefix: Vault holds nine kinds of keys for each zone.

text: Three of them lock what the thief wants to read.
prefix: Three of them lock what the thief wants to read.

text: First, the verified identity of Aziz: his names, passport data, personal identification number and address.
prefix: First, the verified identity of Aziz: his names, passport data, personal identification number and address.

text: His record has its own data key, and that key encrypts the record.
prefix: His record has its own data key, and that key encrypts the record.

text: The data key is stored next to the record, but locked.
prefix: The data key is stored next to the record, but locked.

text: A second key locks it: the key-encryption key of the installation.
prefix: A second key locks it: the key-encryption key of the installation.

text: The key-encryption key never leaves Vault.
prefix: The key-encryption key never leaves Vault.

text: To read the record, the platform sends the locked data key to Vault.
prefix: To read the record, the platform sends the locked data key to Vault.

text: Vault gives it back open for this one request, and the platform then forgets it.
prefix: Vault gives it back open for this one request, and the platform then forgets it.

text: This is envelope encryption: each record has its own key, and only Vault opens the envelope around that key.
prefix: This is envelope encryption: each record has its own key, and only Vault opens the envelope around that key.

text: Vault also records each time it opens a data key.
prefix: Vault also records each time it opens a data key.

text: On the disk, the thief has locked records and locked data keys, and nothing that opens them.
prefix: On the disk, the thief has locked records and locked data keys, and nothing that opens them.

text: Second, search.
prefix: Second, search.

text: The platform must find a customer by his personal identification number, among millions of customers.
prefix: The platform must find a customer by his personal identification number, among millions of customers.

text: But that number is encrypted, so the platform cannot compare it.
prefix: But that number is encrypted, so the platform cannot compare it.

text: So it also keeps a blind index: a fingerprint of the number, made with a secret index key from Vault.
prefix: So it also keeps a blind index: a fingerprint of the number, made with a secret index key from Vault.

text: The same number always gives the same fingerprint, so an exact search still works.
prefix: The same number always gives the same fingerprint, so an exact search still works.

text: A fingerprint never gives back the number.
prefix: A fingerprint never gives back the number.

text: Without the index key, nobody can make a fingerprint at all.
prefix: Without the index key, nobody can make a fingerprint at all.

text: Third, the one-time codes.
prefix: Third, the one-time codes.

text: The platform keeps each code only as a fingerprint, and Lesson 9 shows the rules for codes.
prefix: The platform keeps each code only as a fingerprint, and Lesson 9 shows the rules for codes.

text: A code has only a few digits, so a thief can try every possible code in a moment.
prefix: A code has only a few digits, so a thief can try every possible code in a moment.

text: That is why each fingerprint mixes in a pepper: a secret from Vault that is never on the disk.
prefix: That is why each fingerprint mixes in a pepper: a secret from Vault that is never on the disk.

text: Without the pepper, all those tries give nothing.
prefix: Without the pepper, all those tries give nothing.

text: The other six kinds of keys do different work.
prefix: The other six kinds of keys do different work.

text: One key seals the audit trail, so that a changed record shows, and Lesson 21 shows it.
prefix: One key seals the audit trail, so that a changed record shows, and Lesson 21 shows it.

text: Keycloak signs each token with its own keys, and a secret from Vault encrypts those keys in its database.
prefix: Keycloak signs each token with its own keys, and a secret from Vault encrypts those keys in its database.

text: The credentials of the adapters from Lesson 5 live here too.
prefix: The credentials of the adapters from Lesson 5 live here too.

text: Three more kinds work only between the units of the platform, such as their certificates.
prefix: Three more kinds work only between the units of the platform, such as their certificates.

text: No key is ever in the code, in a log, or in an app on a phone.
prefix: No key is ever in the code, in a log, or in an app on a phone.

text: The passwords on the disk need no key at all.
prefix: The passwords on the disk need no key at all.

text: The platform keeps only a slow, salted fingerprint of each password, and Lesson 11 shows it.
prefix: The platform keeps only a slow, salted fingerprint of each password, and Lesson 11 shows it.

text: There is no key to steal, because there is nothing to decrypt.
prefix: There is no key to steal, because there is nothing to decrypt.

text: Keys also grow old, and the bank sets how often each one changes.
prefix: Keys also grow old, and the bank sets how often each one changes.

text: When the key-encryption key changes, Vault keeps its old versions, and the platform locks the data keys again in the background.
prefix: When the key-encryption key changes, Vault keeps its old versions, and the platform locks the data keys again in the background.

text: Back to the disk.
prefix: Back to the disk.

text: The thief can read the phone number of Aziz, and a few masked parts, such as the last four digits of his document.
prefix: The thief can read the phone number of Aziz, and a few masked parts, such as the last four digits of his document.

text: He cannot read the name, the passport data, the address or the full identification number of Aziz.
prefix: He cannot read the name, the passport data, the address or the full identification number of Aziz.

text: Every key that could open them stays in the Vault of the bank.
prefix: Every key that could open them stays in the Vault of the bank.

text: For the identity of Aziz, the disk is only lost hardware.
prefix: For the identity of Aziz, the disk is only lost hardware.

text: Suppose the thief also guesses the personal identification number of Aziz.
prefix: Suppose the thief also guesses the personal identification number of Aziz.

text: Can he use that guess to find a record on the disk?
prefix: Can he use that guess to find a record on the disk?

text: No: without the index key from Vault, he cannot make the fingerprint, so his guess matches nothing.
prefix: No: without the index key from Vault, he cannot make the fingerprint, so his guess matches nothing.

text: One Vault for each zone, inside the bank, and the bank holds the keys that unlock it.
prefix: One Vault for each zone, inside the bank, and the bank holds the keys that unlock it.

text: Envelope encryption locks each identity, a blind index finds a number without showing it, and a pepper makes the code fingerprints useless to a thief.
prefix: Envelope encryption locks each identity, a blind index finds a number without showing it, and a pepper makes the code fingerprints useless to a thief.

text: No key sits in the code, in a log, or on a phone.
prefix: No key sits in the code, in a log, or on a phone.

text: The mobile bank holds no key, yet it calls heeyID at each step of the journey of Aziz.
